facts.statement: Unlike other life insurance, variable life has a cash value that varies with the performance of investments the owner chooses, typically mutual funds.
facts.quote: Unlike other life insurance, variable life insurance has a cash value that varies depending, in part, on the performance of investments you choose

items.stem: Which type of life insurance has a cash value that changes with the performance of investment options the owner picks from a menu, typically mutual funds?
options: Variable life
Universal life
Whole life
Indexed universal life
items.explanation: Per the SEC, Investor.gov: Variable Life Insurance guide, variable life has a cash value that varies with the performance of investment options the owner chooses, typically mutual funds. Universal life credits interest, indexed universal life ties crediting to an index, and whole life has guaranteed values.

facts.statement: A variable life policyowner can lose money, including the initial investment, if the chosen investments perform poorly.
facts.quote: You can lose money in a variable life insurance policy, including potential loss of your initial investment.

items.stem: If the investment options a variable life policyowner selects perform poorly, the owner:
options: Keeps a guaranteed minimum cash value
Receives a refund of premiums from the insurer
Can lose earnings, but not the initial investment
Could lose money, including the initial investment
items.explanation: Per the SEC, Investor.gov: Variable Life Insurance guide, a variable life policyowner can lose money, including the initial investment, if the chosen investment options perform poorly.

facts.statement: Substantial fees, expenses and tax implications generally make variable life unsuitable as short-term savings.
facts.quote: Substantial fees, expenses, and tax implications generally make variable life insurance unsuitable as a short-term savings vehicle.

items.stem: A client wants somewhere to keep savings for 18 months. Why is variable life insurance generally unsuitable for that goal?
options: High costs and unfavorable tax effects if surrendered early
Its limited choice of death benefit options
Its minimum holding period set by federal law
Its requirement that premiums be paid monthly
items.explanation: Per the SEC, Investor.gov: Variable Life Insurance guide, substantial fees, expenses and tax implications generally make variable life unsuitable as a short-term savings vehicle.
items.retired: Flagged as test-wise in three rounds: unsuitability reasons are hard to write without the key standing out.

facts.statement: Universal life lets the owner vary premium payments and adjust the face amount; increases may require proof of insurability.
facts.quote: Universal LifeInsurance is a kind of flexible policy that lets you vary your premium payments. You can also adjust the face amount of your coverage. Increases may require proof that you qualify for the new death benefit.

items.stem: Which feature most sets universal life apart from traditional whole life?
options: The cash value is tied to separate investment accounts
The premium is guaranteed level for life
The owner can vary premium payments and adjust the face amount
It covers the insured for a set term of years
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, universal life is a flexible policy that lets the owner vary premium payments and adjust the face amount. Increases may require proof of insurability.

facts.statement: If universal life premiums plus interest fall short of the charges, the account value drops, and if it keeps dropping the coverage ends.
facts.quote: If your yearly premium payment plus the interest your account earns is less than the charges, your account value will become lower. If it keeps dropping, eventually your coverage will end.

items.stem: A universal life owner has paid very small premiums for several years, and the interest credited plus her payments have not covered the policy's charges. If this continues, what will happen?
options: The insurer will switch the policy to term at the same premium
The face amount will rise to match the charges
The charges will be waived until interest rates recover
The account value will keep falling until coverage ends
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, when universal life premiums plus interest are less than the charges, the account value falls, and if it keeps dropping, coverage eventually ends.
